pins.definition: Human beings in general, or a person regardless of sex or age.
A human being considered as an individual.
A human being; an individual person.

situation: A museum curator stands alone inside a brightly lit display case, stepping out of a life-sized diagram to show the scale of an individual human being.
subject: a single human individual
brief: A lone woman stands upright inside a tall, open-faced glass exhibit case in a quiet museum hall, illuminated by a spotlight from above. Around her, layered paper cutouts of anatomical and sociological charts frame the space, establishing her clearly as an independent human being.
prompt: A lone woman stands upright inside a tall, open-faced glass exhibit case in a quiet museum hall, illuminated by a spotlight from above. Around her, layered paper cutouts of anatomical and sociological charts frame the space, establishing her clearly as an independent human being. layered cut paper filling the whole frame, real depth between the layers, crisp cast shadows, visibly fibrous card and translucent tissue, raking side light. Never a box, a shadow-box or a picture frame around the scene — the paper IS the world, not an object sitting inside one. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
